Synopsis:
Players use the submersible to travel to the Iron Throne submersed building. On the way, spectator guards meet them and trigger the explosives on the upper dome of the facility. With little time before the prison facilities collapse, the players dock with the station, aiming to save the prisoners before it's destroyed.

Cluster Contexts:
- IRN_IronThrone_Arrival.json: The party is aboard a submersible approaching the submerged Iron Throne complex — a ruined, multi-storey building with a newer domed section on top — and have just docked at a bay on its uppermost level. Off-screen, Lord Gortash remotely contacts the submersible and, angry at the intrusion, activates explosives that detonate around the facility’s upper dome. Spectator/Black Hand guards nearby raise the alarm and are carrying out orders to destroy the Iron Throne, so the facility is rapidly destabilizing. Several glass-walled holding cells on the upper levels contain prisoners (including, depending on prior choices, Grand Duke Ranvegard), and sudden power flickers and structural damage mean the players have only a short window to get them out before the prison collapses.
- IRN_IronThrone_Destruction.json: The Iron Throne is seen collapsing under the water pressure. If players managed to escape, they are seen escaping with the submersible.
- LOW_BellyOfTheBeast_Beastmaster.json: The players have a conversation with the 'beastmaster' - an engineer who operates the Submersible. The player can either be sent here by Allandra to kill the beastmaster, or stumble here after following clues from the Steelwatch Foundry and want a way to get to the Iron Throne. They can also stumble upon it first, before getting any clues about it.The beastmaster works for Gortash, operating the submersible to transfer people and items to and from the Iron Throne The beastmaster can be talked into taking the players to the Iron Throne using the submersible. If he's killed instead, players will have other ways of finding the needed information and/or items to use the submersible on their own.The beastmaster should make it clear that he would not step out into the Iron Throne itself.
- WYR_GortashConfrontation_OM_KarlachAndGortashEncounter_AOM_OOM.json: Dialog with Gortash in his office.Possible outcomes:1. You visited Steel Foundry and the destroyed Control Centre - he attacks you.2. You visited Steel Foundry, didn't destroy the Control Centre, but someone activated Dead Man switch which destroyed Iron T hrone. He attacks you.3. You visited Iron Throne which caused the destruction of it. He tells you - "I warned you" and then attacks you.4. You didn't kill Orin.5. You killed Orin and you have both Netherstones.6. Fallback node which includes the case where you killed Orin, but didn't bring either of the netherstones.
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_Confrontation_AfterIRN.json: This dialog plays if the player solves the Iron Throne before ever seeing the LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_DeadMansSwitchThreat dialog.After destroying the Iron Throne the player walks in Baneites tormenting Gondian Workers in the Foundry Work room.With the Iron Throne gone, the dead mans switch no longer works.

context: The party is aboard a submersible that has just docked at a bay on the Iron Throne’s topmost, domed level. Off-screen, Lord Gortash has remotely contacted the vessel and pressed a detonator, setting explosives that rupture the upper dome and send the facility into rapid structural failure. Spectator/Black Hand guards nearby are raising the alarm and carrying out orders to destroy the Iron Throne, while power flickers and debris rains through the upper levels. Several glass-walled holding cells contain prisoners (which may include Grand Duke Ranvegard depending on prior choices), so the players have only a short window to get people out before the prison collapses. The submersible’s engineer—the beastmaster who works for Gortash—operates the craft and will not step out onto the Iron Throne, making the submersible the party’s only means of extraction.
